title: A Drop of Honey
coreMove: Open a hard conversation with sincere warmth before you raise the disagreement, and keep that warmth in your voice until the other person has stopped bracing.

exampleSpecs.domain: a landlord knocking on a tenant's door at 9pm to complain about a months-overdue rent check
exampleSpecs.audience: a small-property landlord who has rehearsed an angry speech in the car
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the tenant pays this week or digs in for an eviction fight that will cost the landlord three months of rent
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the landlord drops the prepared opener, asks first about the tenant's sick mother whose name he actually remembers, and only later mentions the check — and watches the tenant's shoulders come down before any money is discussed

exampleSpecs.domain: a labor negotiator walking into a wage talk after a bitter strike vote the night before
exampleSpecs.audience: a union representative who expects to be greeted as the enemy
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the talks open with a shouting match or a workable opening offer
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the company's negotiator opens by naming, by name, two workers whose grievances were legitimate, and the union rep audibly hesitates before reading his prepared statement

exampleSpecs.domain: a high school orchestra conductor confronting a violinist who has been late to three rehearsals in a row
exampleSpecs.audience: a public-school music teacher with twenty other students watching
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the violinist quits the orchestra or goes back to playing first stand
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the conductor walks the student into the hallway, says one true sentence about the student's tone last Thursday, and only then asks what is going on at home

exampleSpecs.domain: a grown daughter calling her father to tell him he should not be driving anymore
exampleSpecs.audience: a daughter in her forties who has dreaded this call for a year
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the father takes her seriously or hangs up insulted and keeps the keys out of spite
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the daughter notices her own throat tightening, hears herself almost lead with the accident report, and instead opens with a memory of him teaching her to parallel park — choosing warmth not as a tactic but because it is the truer first thing to say

exampleSpecs.domain: a head chef telling a line cook the soup he has made every Tuesday for six years is being taken off the menu
exampleSpecs.audience: a head chef in a sixty-seat restaurant
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the cook keeps showing up or walks out mid-shift on a Friday
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the first attempt is a curt announcement at family meal that costs the kitchen its best sauté hand for two days; the second attempt, weeks later with a different cut, begins with the chef thanking the cook in front of the staff for a specific save during last summer's heatwave

exampleSpecs.domain: a homeowner trying to get a neighbor to stop letting her terrier dig under the fence
exampleSpecs.audience: someone who has rewritten the same text message four times
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the next ten years on this street are friendly or frosty
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the homeowner sits at the kitchen table, deletes the draft that begins 'I've asked you repeatedly,' and writes one that opens by remembering the neighbor's kindness during the ice storm — and notices her own anger softening as she writes it, which is the point
